item.title: Her Last Call To Her Sister Was From Walmart
item.description: Caitlin Denison, 19, called her sister from a Midland, Texas, Walmart in January 2018, saying she feared for her life after traveling there with a man. Her sister recalls that final conversation as Texas Rangers continue investigating her unresolved disappearance.

item.title: He Spent 37 Hours Covering Up Her Murder
item.description: Christine Holloway, 43, was killed in Ansonia, Connecticut, in December 2019. Trial evidence showed Jose Morales spent 37 hours cleaning up and destroying evidence. He received 65 years for murder and evidence tampering in 2025. Their daughter Vanessa, then 14 months old, remains missing.

item.title: She Called 911 About An Intruder Her Husband Invented
item.description: Heidi Firkus, 25, was shot during a 911 call in St. Paul in 2010. Her husband Nicholas blamed an intruder, but investigators uncovered an eviction scheduled for the next day that he had concealed from her. Convicted of murder in 2023, he received life without parole; his conviction was upheld in 2026.

item.title: Three Overlooked Polaroids Unraveled Mark Winger’s Story
item.description: Mark Winger claimed he shot an intruder attacking his wife, Donnah, in their Illinois home in 1995. Overlooked crime-scene photos contradicted his account. In 2002, he was convicted of murdering both Donnah and shuttle driver Roger Harrington and sentenced to life without parole.

item.title: The Missing Lawyer Whose Wife Wasn’t Who She Claimed
item.description: California attorney Larry McNabney vanished in 2001. When investigators uncovered his death from horse tranquilizer, they also exposed his wife “Elisa” as Laren Sims, a fugitive using an alias. She confessed but died before trial; accomplice Sarah Dutra was convicted of voluntary manslaughter.

item.title: His Body Was Found Where Searchers Had Already Looked
item.description: Kurt Sova, 17, disappeared after an Ohio party in October 1981. Five days later, his body was found in a previously searched ravine. Police said the coroner estimated he had been dead less than 24 hours but could not establish why he died. The case remains unresolved.

item.title: She Went Upstairs To Model A Dress And Never Returned
item.description: Eight months pregnant, Savanna LaFontaine-Greywind, 22, disappeared after visiting her upstairs neighbor in Fargo in August 2017. Police found her baby alive in the neighbor’s apartment. Brooke Crews pleaded guilty to conspiring to murder Savanna and kidnap her baby, receiving life without parole.
